#1601. Opinion: Liverpool concerns prove that exciting star is on his way to Anfield

Liverpool haven't been at their best this season.

Whether that's because their players have failed to meet expectations or if its because they've just not got enough shots off, Andoni Iraola's men just haven't been at the races this term.

They've lost a fair few games across all competitions and, without some serious reinforcement in the upcoming transfer windows, they're going to fall even further behind their title rivals.

Obviously, a team of Liverpool's stature should be challenging for silverware every season but, at this rate, that's almost certainly not going to happen.

But, with how many players the Reds have been linked with recently, it's good news to see that some of those deals could now end up being confirmed.

Liverpool have concerns over Milos Kerkez's recent form

Milos Kerkez has probably been one of Liverpool's worst performers this season.

The Hungarian has failed to meet expectations on numerous occasions and, even though there have been times when his talent has shone through, it has often felt like the Reds made the wrong choice when they sold Andy Robertson in the summer.

Indeed, Kostas Tsimikas is another option that the Anfield outfit have but, somehow, he's been even worse than Kerkez.

These poor performances have led to fans questioning whether a new left-back should be on top of Liverpool's shortlist or not.

And now, thanks to a fresh update from Football Insider, it's clear that Liverpool are also thinking the same way.

"Liverpool are beginning to develop concerns about Milos Kerkez's displays so far this season, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote.

"The 22-year-old has retained his position as the starting left-back this season, and has started ten games across all competitions so far, including eight in the Premier League.

"However, his inconsistent displays have led to question marks about his long-term role in the side, and whether Liverpool will need to strengthen in his position.

"Andoni Iraola is a big fan of the Hungary international, who he also worked with at Bournemouth, and has been backed to get him back to his best in the near future."

Liverpool's concerns over Milos Kerkez could lead to them signing Alejandro Balde in January

Several left-backs have been linked with a Liverpool move this season.

Although none of them ended up joining in the summer, many rumours have emerged linking Liverpool with a January move for one or two players.

Among those linked, Barcelona's Alejandro Balde has been a well recieved move by fans.

The 23-year-old was Hansi Flick's starting left-back last term but, for one reason or another, he's been left on the bench this term.

Balde's natural position is at left-back but, during the start of his Barcelona career, he also played a handful of games at right-back.

The La Liga giants only want around £34 million for Balde so a deal for him would be cheap and, since he's already proven that he can handle the Champions League and can contribute to the team well, it feels like a deal for the Spaniard is a no-brainer.

That is, especially if there are concerns about the future of Kerkez in L4.

#1598. Man City's slump cannot be excused by guilty verdict: Too many blunders, too much arm waving and football problems are piling up after 3-1 defeat by Nottingham Forest, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 14:52 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:21 EST, 7 November 2026

This run will not be about the verdicts. This cannot be about the verdicts. Footballers do not care about these things, the stuff out of their control. Besides, all of them are earning cut-price transfers elsewhere were Manchester City to suffer relegation anyway. And cut-price fees mean bulkier salaries.

So to them the current climate, the circumstances around City – their recent history and their immediate future – does not overly matter. Sure, there might be the odd one who is slightly more philosophical and inquisitive about appeals and appendices but the majority won't be giving it much or any thought.

City insist on their innocence publicly and privately; until that changes, their players and Enzo Maresca carry on regardless. There were the usual jeers here, there were ditties about cheating, but that surely cannot affect them.

Instead, the performances over the past few weeks, this a third consecutive Premier League defeat and now sinking six points adrift of Arsenal, cannot be excused by the findings of an independent commission. The problems are football problems.

This is a squad who appear uncertain about specific aspects of their game. Namely how to build from the back – and that is prompting individual mistakes. It happened against Ipswich Town and at Aston Villa. On the river Trent, it was no different.

The statistics say City dominated another game and they deserved more but the eyes tell another story.

Man City are a squad who now appear uncertain about specific aspects of their game

The statistics say City dominated another game and they deserved more but the eyes tell another story

Three defeats in a row have seen Enzo Maresca's side slip six points behind leaders Arsenal

Too many errors. Too much arm waving. Too much feeling sorry for themselves when decisions go elsewhere. Oliver Glasner is not stupid, he will have seen examples of this play out in parts of City's victories as well as reverses.

As Liam Delap raced into the corner to celebrate his second with 17 minutes left – a huge day in his career against the club which moulded him – Glasner was dashing down the touchline with unbridled joy.

Nottingham Forest (5-2-2-1): Sels 6; Munoz 6 (Netz 65, 6), Cunha 8, Milenkovic 8, Murillo 7, Williams 8; Yates 8 (Sangare 79), Schlager 8; McAtee 7 (Ndoye 65, 6), Gibbs-White 7; Delap 9 (Jesus 87)

Man City (4-1-4-1): Donnarumma 5; Khusanov 5, Dias 5, Guehi 4 (Nunes 46, 7), Gvardiol 4 (O'Reilly 46, 6); Anderson 5; Ndiaye 6, Cherki 6, Fernandez 4 (Foden 78), Doku 6; Haaland 5

Forest displays have deserved more than their points total so far and this was vindication for their fifth manager in 14 months, who suggested he fancied sampling Nottingham’s nightlife afterwards. Delap was exceptional, some personal redemption after criticism.

The way in which Glasner nudged James McAtee further forward, stationed higher from the off in order to pressurise the visitors, spoke to an idea that City arrived here ready to be ruffled and have been wearing a look of fragility.

By the time this was eight minutes shy of half time and McAtee was nicking possession from Elliot Anderson, drawing a foul that sparked another onslaught on Gianluigi Donnarumma's box, Forest were already two clear – and had been for some time. Phil Foden warmed up on the touchline, laughing and hugging with Callum Hudson-Odoi.

Forest preyed on City insecurities. A midfield structure that is simply not working at the moment, easily railroaded. A defence allergic to the basics and an epidemic of individual mistakes – either as a result of nervousness or blase attitude on the ball.

Straight to the mistakes. A real collection, these: the first in the fifth minute and the others 13 minutes afterwards. Jair Cunha wheeled away after picking Josko Gvardiol's pocket, meandering forward into the box and side-footing into the far corner largely unchallenged. Gvardiol seemed to have the air of a man who felt invincible when gathering possession before being eased off it.

Later, as Delap thundered forward 45 yards unchecked to hammer past Donnarumma, you wondered about the communication between these City players. Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye left things to each other near halfway, Xaver Schlager gave his thanks – finding Delap – and the City academy graduate bulldozed clear. Marc Guehi waved him through, Ruben Dias dithered and Maresca bowed his head.

Liam Delap was exceptional for Nottingham Forest, some personal redemption after criticism

Remarkably, this was the first time in seven years that City had gone two down inside 18 minutes

Remarkably, this was the first time in seven years that City had gone two down inside 18 minutes. Dias looked aghast at Guehi, who was then hooked at the break alongside Gvardiol. Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki both stood in the centre circle, hands on hips.

It later emerged via replays that Anderson had been arguing with Abdukodir Khusanov in the build-up to Forest's opener as well, proof that City were nowhere near close to producing what was expected when on the ball in their own half.

Glasner had the weapons at his disposal to make this work but even the Austrian must have been surprised at the way in which they tickled City's soft underbelly. They had not scored at the City Ground all season. All change when owner Evangelos Marinakis made his first trip to see a game since Glasner's appointment, which felt particularly handy, with Yates having delivered a spinetingling dressing room speech pre-match.

Anger permeated the eyes of some City players as the whistle went. Cherki stormed down the tunnel, animatedly discussing how to play through Forest with Fernandez when they re-emerged.

Their lifeline came after 52 minutes, a Ryan Yates deflection from Jeremy Doku's cross sitting up for Cherki to hammer home a half-volley off the bar. Doku soon almost squeezed another effort past Matz Sels and the mood shifted, City briefly creeping menacingly like the monsters they are portrayed as.

Maresca had introduced Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly, with both affecting the upturn. An admission of selection errors, perhaps, although O'Reilly is managing an ongoing back issue and is set for therapy on it over the international break.

City will need some of that as a collective. Delap won the ball inside his own third, gliding past Anderson, and Forest's explosive counter ended with Delap spearing a shot in off the post after Morgan Gibbs-White carried possession unopposed for 60 yards. Delirium, Glasner darting to the corner flag.

The quirk of this is that City's failings mean Manchester United drop into the bottom three.

Maresca criticised Manchester City’s lack of fight but insisted that City created enough chances to leave with something despite admitting his players were physically second best.

‘In the first half we were not good enough - we didn't match the intensity that these kind of games require,’ Maresca said.

‘If you are not able to win the second balls then you struggle. You have to match the desire to win second balls and duels, otherwise it is not good. When you lost balls the way we did and cannot recover immediately, it’s a matter of winning duels.’

Maresca has a two-week international break to rake over the issues affecting his side and believes time away could do the squad good.

The Italian added: ‘When you lose a game you always want to go again immediately to try to win games but I think that this international break, the last one until March, is also good for the players.

‘We didn't match the intensity. We need to understand the reason why and try to avoid the next games. There is no panic. We need to understand but no panic.’

Maresca revealed that defenders Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol asked to come off at half time with injuries, while Forest out-ran his team by 6km on the night.

‘If you want to win against City, you need to do this,’ Oliver Glasner said after recording his first home win. ‘Credit to Liam, these strikes are something you have or you don't have.

‘It can be a turning point but we have to prove it. The way we performed today should give us confidence.’

City winger Jeremy Doku could not explain why they could not deal with Forest before half time.

‘We are used to playing every two days - that's not a reason,’ Doku said. ‘If you ask me for the reason for our first half I don't know.

‘We reacted too late. We need to be fresh minds, start again and analyse what we can do better and move forward. The international break comes at the right moment for us to analyse and come back refreshed.’

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

“I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

“This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He said: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”

Tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel said. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

“It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

“So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I said, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”

Tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always said he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”

Tuchel said that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”

Tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

It was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

“I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“I don’t have a clear picture on what he is all about and have a very clear picture on what Levi can bring us.”

“It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

“It’s one thing to be nominated, but it’s another thing to perform. This also counts, especially Cole needs to step up to justify the nomination.”

“The minimum I can do is back my bosses. They have my full support on that.

“I’m grateful that I can talk about football because that’s my little bit of knowledge, not sports politics.”

“That’s the beauty of high-level sport, you can’t always win and it makes you feel alive. Not in a very nice way, still you feel that pain of these high-pressure moments.

“As soon as you enter knockout football, it’s a new level of pressure.”

Tuchel has now claimed that people say the 6-4 against France is “maybe one of their best experiences (watching football) ever”.

Again, not something anyone has said to me. Where is Tuchel finding these people?!

Tuchel on Alexander-Arnold: “He comes as a right back.” Sounds like he agrees with Mourinho that the Real Madrid player is not a midfielder.

Tuchel: “There was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their (the FA’s) mind.”

Tuchel says that 99.9 per cent of fans don’t talk about substitutions. He says they speak about the Mexico game and the Croatia game, their emotions and where they watched the matches.

Sorry, Thomas, that’s not my experience at all. Everyone I speak to says he blew the Argentina game. This sounds a bit deluded. According to Tuchel, I must speak to 0.01 per cent of England fans....

FA technical director John McDermott, who has taken a position at the back of the room to listen, had a little laugh when Tuchel joked that he got told off in his FA review for “my substitutions.”

Tuchel says he felt the “full support from my bosses”.

Warning for Palmer: “It’s one thing to get your ticket back, but it’s another thing to keep it.”

He’s expecting Palmer to step up and show him his Chelsea form.

“When you are a coach, you only win when you win...There’s not much sense torturing ourselves by looking back. I will not allow 30 minutes of the World Cup to determine how we view the World Cup.”

Tuchel says he has no regrets over not taking Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup. He says he didn’t have a single sleepless night over his squad selection.

Tuchel says the direction in sports is always forwards and never backwards. “The target is to win the home Euros, of course.”

Tuchel says his feelings on the World Cup are mixed. He thinks there are very positive things to take from the World Cup, but says it was also unfulfilled. He says it’s important to recognise that England won a bronze medal, but says he acknowledges they did not push it over the line.

He says the downside of having the belief they could go and win it is that it hurts even more that they did not.

Tuchel has said the France third-place game “directs the narrative” of what’s coming for England.

Tuchel will be happy with this so far. Very gentle start from the broadcasters.

Ben White pulled out with an injury after being back to his best. It is unfortunately, a bit of a story for him. Josh King was very close and is on the radar.

Tuchel seems to be referring to notes as he speaks. He keeps looking down at a piece of paper he brought in with him.

“The door is always open through performance, behaviour and commitment.”

#1594. Rabiot hits out at refereeing after Marcandalli incident: “Constantly lying won’t achieve progress”

Adrien Rabiot has had his say on the incident that happened during AC Milan’s win over Genoa, in which he was brought down through on goal.

The controversial moment everyone is talking about came early in the second half. Rabiot pressured Marcandalli and stole the ball off him and he was about to surge into Genoa’s half, with only Alphadjo Cisse to his left for company in a two-on-zero breakaway.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Marcandalli hauled him down, yet the referee Davide Massa only saw fit to award a yellow card, and the VAR chief did not deem it necessary to call him over to the monitor for another look. Milan won anyway in the end, but it would have been a totally different game had that been given.

Former referee Gianpaolo Calvarese commented on the incident on his Instagram page and he described Marcandalli’s yellow card as a ‘fair’ decision, which prompted Rabiot to respond in the comments.

“In life, as in football, you can make mistakes. You have to at least be able to admit them. Constantly lying won’t achieve progress, and Italian football is the one that suffers the consequences. Think about it. Bonne soirée,” the Frenchman said.

A post shared by Gianpaolo Calvarese (@gianpaolocalvarese_official)

The relationship between Rabiot and Italian referees has always been characterised by a direct, unfiltered approach. The former PSG man has never been one to hide when he feels he’s suffered an injustice.

He demonstrated this during his time at Juventus. In April 2022, after the defeat against Inter he wrote on Instagram: “It’s difficult to play with 11 against 12.” A year later, in Juventus-Sevilla, he protested again over a denied penalty, even showing the media the marks left by the studs on his leg.

Rabiot brought this to Milan too. After the match against Atalanta on October 18th, for example, he questioned the awarding of bookings, complaining about several uncalled fouls, leading to his famous celebration in front of Chiffi when he scored the 2-0 goal.

#1593. Virgil van Dijk injury explained as Liverpool captain pulls out of Netherlands squad

By Ben Sully | 10 Nov 2026 01:14, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 01:14

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has been ruled out of the Netherlands' upcoming Nations League games due to injury.

Van Dijk was named in Xavi's squad for the final two matches of the league phase, with the Oranje battling Greece and Germany for a top-two finish in Group A2.

The Netherlands will face Greece in Amsterdam on Friday before they head to Berlin for Monday's meeting with Germany.

However, they will go into those two games without Van Dijk, who has withdrawn from the squad along with Sunderland forward Brian Brobbey.

In a statement released on Monday, the Dutch football association said: "Virgil van Dijk and Brian Brobbey aren’t fit enough to feature in the upcoming Nations League matches. No replacements will be called up."

Van Dijk's withdrawal came just a day after he played the full duration of Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park.

According to journalist James Pearce, the Liverpool skipper has been playing with a minor injury problem in recent weeks.

While the nature of the issue has not been disclosed, the decision to withdraw from the squad has evidently been taken to avoid aggravating the problem.

Liverpool fans will likely be pleased with the news of Van Dijk's withdrawl, given that he will now get the chance to rest and recuperate over the next two weeks.

Despite being 35, Van Dijk's importance to Liverpool has shown no signs of waning under Andoni Iraola this term.

The Dutchman has played over 1,200 minutes, having started 14 of his 15 appearances in all competitions.

Liverpool will want Van Dijk raring to go for a tricky run of fixtures that will see the Reds face Manchester United, Everton and Chelsea in the space of four Premier League games after the international break.

According to The Telegraph, Dyche is among the leading candidates should Palace decide to part ways with Sage.

The 55-year-old has been without a managerial position since leaving Nottingham Forest in February. His experience in Premier League survival battles could appeal to Palace as they attempt to turn their season around.

Dyche previously established his reputation at Burnley, guiding the club into the Premier League and keeping them in the top flight for several seasons. He also helped Everton avoid relegation during his time at Goodison Park.

Despite the speculation, Sage has maintained that he believes the players and club hierarchy remain behind him. His immediate challenge is to improve results and ease fears of a relegation battle.

What this means for Crystal Palace: Dyche’s experience makes him a reported option if Palace decide to change direction. However, no appointment has been confirmed, and Sage’s future remains dependent on the club’s next decision.

#1591. Sheffield Wednesday vs Accrington Stanley - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 10 Nov 2026 01:41

Sheffield Wednesday will go in search of a first victory under the new management of Dave Challinor on Wednesday, when they welcome Accrington Stanley to Hillsborough for an EFL Trophy contest.

Wednesday's game will round off the group stage with the hosts already through and the visitors knowing a point would guarantee their knockout place.

Sheffield Wednesday head into their second game under Dave Challinor on Wedensday aiming to get up and running with their new boss after an FA Cup exit at the weekend.

The South Yorkshire have returned to this competition after relegation to League One last time around, but they looked set for a fresh start in the third tier having come out of administration under prior ownership which saw them end 2025-26 on 0 points.

Sticking with manager Henrik Pedersen initially with fresh ownership and a much-improved squad, immediately putting themselves among the division's frontrunners while also winning their first two EFL Trophy games 2-1 and 2-0 against Salford City and Sunderland Under-21s respectively.

Pedersen's tenure would come to an end following back-to-back league defeats in October, and on the back of a draw against Blackpool under caretaker manager Matt Hamshaw, they turned to Challinor who began on Sunday in an FA Cup tie away at fourth-tier Oldham Athletic, in which the Owls lost 2-1 after extra time with Davis Keillor-Dunn levelling in normal time and Will Sutton scoring the decisive goal.

Now already guaranteed a place in the EFL Trophy knockout rounds thanks to their opening two wins, but keen to rebuild confidence and kickstart their new era having dropped to ninth spot in League One, Sheffield Wednesday will look to complete a perfect group-stage record with a home win on Wednesday.

In their way stand an Accrington Stanley team who are close to securing their own place in the knockout stage of the EFL Trophy.

The visitors have come out on top in both of their first two EFL Trophy group games, albeit not taking full points in either, as they firstly drew 3-3 against Sunderland Under-21s thanks to Stefan Mols's injury-time leveller and won a penalty shootout.

John Doolan's team again took a second point when they played Salford City and drew 1-1 with David Tutonda scoring another equaliser deep into injury time, with both of those results forming part of a 10-game unbeaten streak which also saw them climb to ninth spot in League Two.

Aiming to extend that further in the first of consecutive cup games, the Reds hosted third-tier Wycombe Wanderers in the FA Cup first round on Saturday and fell to a first loss since mid-September as Connor Taylor and Dan Harvie scored in a 2-0 away triumph.

Now left to focus on the EFL Trophy with a three-point lead over Salford City and Sunderland Under-21s, who play one another in the final round of games, Accrington Stanley will go in search of a statement result at Hillsborough to confirm their place in the next round.

Sheffield Wednesday form (all competitions):

Accrington Stanley form (all competitions):

Sheffield Wednesday will be without second-choice goalkeeper Ashley Maynard-Brewer, who was forced off early against Oldham last time out, joining fellow stopper Joe Lumley in the treatment room alongside the likes of Liam Cooper, Tyler Onyango, Louie Barry and Ali Al-Hamadi.

In the place of Maynard-Brewer, who only recently came in in place of Lumley, Connal Trueman will deputise between the sticks, while Challinor may make some rotations with the Owls' place in the next stage already confirmed.

He may afford rests for Barry Bannan and Callum Slattery, while Di'Shon Bernard may continue in defence as his return to full fitness from a long-term injury continues, and Kieran Morrison, Sean Fusire, Jarvis Thornton and Ernie Weaver are among those hoping to earn starts.

Accrington Stanley remain unable to call on attacker Charlie Caton, who has been sidelined since scoring five goals in his first seven League One appearances of the season.

Seamus Conneely, Liam Coyle and Josh Woods have also picked up injuries in the last month, while Kelsey Mooney and Isaac Sinclair are yet to feature this season as they remain confined to the treatment room.

In the absence of Woods and Caton, the attack should again be led by Charlie Warren, who has scored five goals this season, and Tyler Walton, who netted a brace in a recent 5-0 win over Rochdale.

Sheffield Wednesday possible starting lineup:

Trueman; Weaver, Santos, Bernard; Fusire, Heskey, Thornton, Liongola; Morrison, Lowe, Gray

Accrington Stanley possible starting lineup:

Moulden; Matthews, Rawson, Anderson; Whalley, Mols, Borland, Grant; Darcy; Warren, Walto

Accrington Stanley have the tools to hurt Sheffield Wednesday, particularly given the hosts' slight rut and likelihood of rotatin, but keen to get a first win under Challinor we do ultimately see the Owls making their extra quality count and bouncing back to winning ways.

#1588. Martin Odegaard sends Arsenal six clear at the top: The stylists and aesthetes will moan - but Mikel Arteta can rest easy over the international break, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI

By RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 12:30 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:22 EST, 7 November 2026

Arsenal are building a wall around their precious trophy with ugly bricks. While the stylists and aesthetes among us can moan about such details, a quick glance at the league table will be sufficient for Mikel Arteta to rest easy during the international break.

There are certainly things for him to improve. Masses of them. And we can all share the disappointment that the sum of such gifted parts is often quite underwhelming. There's a relentlessness about that conversation.

But Arsenal are relentless in other ways, too. Which is to say they are finding ways to win, with this their ninth in ten games and arguably the least convincing of an unconvincing bunch.

If Manchester City weren't facing up to the possibility of an apocalyptic punishment, those performances would likely cause greater concern but it's a tangential argument. A purist's debate. And by extension it is pointless against the single factor that matters most – scoring more than the other lot.

In this case, grimy as it was, that crowning role fell to Martin Odegaard, who nudged the winner over the line in the 72nd minute after benefiting from a favourable rebound after Konstantinos Tzolakis had saved from Noni Madueke.

The latter is surfing ever faster on the wave of his current form and impressed throughout this match, but his wing play and the resilience of Arteta's back four warranted isolated praise.

Martin Odegaard secured Arsenal's fourth Premier League win in succession against Hull

The Gunners had been frustrated by the newly-promoted side before Odegaard pounced

For all of Arsenal's grumbles about the officiating, including a bizarre penalty claim for Kai Havertz in the first half, they were poor, even if most sides would trade an arm for four straight clean sheets and a healthy lead in the table.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Raya 6; Timber 7, Konsa 7, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie 69, 7); Rice 6 (Merino 63, 7), Guimaraes 5 (Zubimendi 89); Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 69, 6); Havertz 5 (Gyokeres 63, 6)

Subs not used: Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Lewis-Skelly

Hull (5-3-2-): Tzolakis 7; Coyle 6 (Norton-Cuffy 60, 5), Ajayi 7 (Herrington 69, 6), Egan 7, Mendy 6, Stroud 7 (Giles 75, 6); Iroegbunam 7 (Mouzakitis 75, 6), Gourna-Douath 7, Slater 7; McBurnie 6, Cho 5 (Gelhardt 60, 6)

Subs not used: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Hjerto-Dahl, Vaz

For the majority of the first 45 minutes, this game was shaped by Hull, who hadn't won since August. They had drawn five of their previous seven games and given up winning positions in four of them, but Sergej Jakirovic is doing good work. Here, he had Arteta baffled for long stretches and elements of his blueprint will have been noted by future opposition.

Jakirovic's intentions had been clear, both on the team sheet and the pitch. He kept with his default setting for a back five, but switched from a 5-4-1 to 5-3-2 and introduced Mohamed-Ali Cho to partner Oli McBurnie in attack.

It was the first time this season that Hull's manager has used a front two and dovetailed with his midweek warning that camping on the edge of their area would lead nowhere but trouble. Instead, the aim was to squeeze, suffocate and chase the champions at every turn. That worked for an hour for Leeds and it did likewise for Hull.

Inside the first 70 seconds, they had forced a corner. A moment later, John Egan outjumped Gabriel Magalhaes and headed into the side netting.

Soon enough, David Raya was forced into a save by Regan Slater. In landing a shot on target, Hull had achieved a greater threat after 18 minutes than Liverpool delivered in the entire 90 at Anfield last weekend.

It was strong stuff. And ballsy. Arsenal had space to exploit at the other end but that was contingent on having the composure to pick the right pass. For an awfully long time, that eluded them.

Christos Tzolis and Havertz each offered the limpest of protests for early penalties and Declan Rice belatedly caused some threat with a half-volley. For a while, that was as good as it got, before a third penalty appeal arrived. This one was contentious.

Arsenal were denied a penalty following a shirt pull on centre forward Kai Havertz

Mikel Arteta demands a free kick in Arsenal's favour on a frustrating afternoon in north London

Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal must be more 'chaotic' and ruthless after wasting multiple chances in their 1-0 victory over Hull City.

Martin Odegaard's second-half strike sealed a fifth consecutive Premier League victory for the Gunners going into the international break, though his side were initially frustrated by the stubborn visitors.

'I'm delighted with the win because to go into the international break after winning is one of the best things for a coach or a player,' said Arteta.

'I think we were the better team and had enough chances to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren't efficient enough to do that.

'We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic.

'Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks. We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And score much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game.'

Arsenal also had a penalty shout turned down in the first period after Kai Havertz's shirt was pulled in the box by Nobel Mendy.

The decision was not given on field, though the VAR told referee Farai Hallam to look at the pitchside monitor.

Hallam announced that Havertz had been fouled, but the forward had been in an offside position.

On the incident, Arteta said: 'I haven't watched it back. I was surprised because when they sent the referee to the monitor, Benji (White) was telling me it's a clear penalty.

'So I heard now that they decided not to (give a penalty) because of the starting position of Kai, that he was offside. So I don't know what the interpretation is. I'm sure they (Pro Ref) will make that clear to understand it.

'I need to understand the decision, what is overruling what in terms of the decision making and after that I can give you an answer.'

The offence traced to a clear shirt-pull by Nobel Mendy on Havertz, with referee Farai Hallam subsequently called to the screen to check if it merited a foul. Returning to the field and engaging his microphone, he confirmed it did but added that Havertz was in an offside position. The verdict: a Hull free-kick.

A word on Hallam – he was the referee who also overruled the VAR on his Premier League debut last season. It's good to see an official who backs his own judgment, so fair play, but was he in the right?

Such is the mess engulfing the laws on offside, an argument could be put forward that, according to the regulations, the foul must take precedence over the offside as Havertz wasn't yet challenging for the ball. A counterpoint: it's an absurd law that is far too subjective.

None of which helped Arsenal, of course. Not for the first time, they were struggling to utilise their creative talents, with Rice and Odegaard swamped in the middle and their supply lines to Tzolis almost non-existent. Madueke created his own threats, but with limited support. When Havertz had a decent opening late in the half, he took one touch too many and allowed Mendy to challenge. It was bleak.

Kicking his heels on the bench was Viktor Gyokeres, who had one of his finest Arsenal performances at Slavia Prague on Wednesday. His reward for a goal and an assist was one of those soul-crushing demotions for Premier League business, and he wasn't introduced here for more than an hour.

By then, Arsenal had asserted some control. Tzolis was drawing countless fouls, including one from Lewie Coyle that ought to have drawn a second yellow card as Hull's pressure strayed closer to brute force. Their grip on a point was loosening.

First, Madueke drew a save from Tzolakis and then he forced another after skipping around Elliot Stroud and pulling the trigger. This one proved decisive because the save rebounded to Odegaard. He poached the winner.

Madueke then ought to have killed the match, but opted to round Tzolakis instead of taking on the shot when through. The keeper won that battle; Arsenal won the game. Ultimately, not much else mattered.

#1587. Barnsley vs Oldham Athletic - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 10 Nov 2026 02:26

In the final round of fixtures in the EFL Trophy group stage, Oldham Athletic will head to Oakwell to take on Barnsley.

The visitors are on the back of an FA Cup victory over Sheffield Wednesday at the weekend and are already qualified for the knockout rounds, while their hosts are unable to progress.

Barnsley return to action at Oakwell on Wednesday aiming to build on a much-needed cup victory at the weekend, albeit while being unable to progress in the EFL Trophy in their final group outing.

After the return of promotion-winning manager Daniel Stendel over the summer, the South Yorkshire outfit have endured a poor start to their League One campaign, currently sitting 23rd having earned just nine points from their first 12 outings and only won two of those alongside seven defeats.

Those wins came consecutively with the most recent being the beginning of September, before the Reds went on an 11-game winless run in all competitions including nine losses, culminating in four straight league defeats and a draw against Oxford United.

Non-league Aldershot then visited Oakwell in the FA Cup first round at the weekend, and Stendel's side finally ended their rut in comfortable fashion, progressing with a 7-2 victory as Cameron McGeehan netted a hat-trick alongside Vimal Yoganathan's brace and goals from Reyes Cleary and Rylan Brownlie.

Now unable to progress in the EFL Trophy, having lost their first two games to Leeds United Under-21s and Fleetwood Town in the midst of their rut, but needing to rebuild confidence before their return to league action in a bid to escape the drop zone, Barnsley will hope to make it back-to-back home cup wins on Wednesday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, arrive in South Yorkshire in search of another cup win over third-tier opposition having already booked their place in the knockout stage of the EFL Trophy.

In their second season back in the EFL, after a 10th-placed League Two finish last time around and an EFL Trophy group-stage exit, Oldham Athletic currently sit 18th in England's fourth tier having won four and lost seven of their first 14 outings.

That is alongside a perfect start to the new EFL Trophy campaign, as they guaranteed a top-two group finish with a 1-0 home win over Fleetwood Town and a 4-2 triumph over Leeds United Under-21s.

Micky Mellon's side are now on the back of consecutive victories too, firstly returning to winning ways in the league last week by beating Northampton Town away from home, before hosting third-tier Sheffield Wednesday in the FA Cup at the weekend and winning 2-1 after extra time with Callum Kavanagh putting them ahead in normal time and Will Sutton scoring the decisive goal in the 110th minute.

Oldham Athletic now head into a second straight cup game in search of another victory to finish the group stage with a perfect record before turning their focus back to climbing up the League Two table.

Desperate for consecutive wins, Stendel will field a similar starting XI from the weekend's cup win, with Ben Hamed Toure and Fabio Jalo still out.

Brownlie may come in from the start after his goal off the bench, while McGeehan and Yoganathan will support a lone striker again after scoring three and two goals respectively at the weekend.

They should again join danger man Reyes Cleary, while Daniel Johnson joined Luca Connell in midfield on Saturday while Patrick Kelly was rested from the start.

Oldham may also be unchanged from their FA Cup victory with Ryan Delaney and Keenan Appiah-Forson still among those sidelined.

Kavanagh will continue to lead the line after his opener against Sheffield Wednesday with Mike Fondop regularly joining him up top.

Injuries and suspensions left the Latics unable to complete their bench on Saturday, meaning the likes of Oliver Norburn and Tom Pett may not be afforded rests.

Slicker; Okedina, Gale, Kay, Larkeche; Connell, Kelly; Yoganathan, McGeehan, Cleary; Adeyemo

Oldham Athletic possible starting lineup:

Hudson; Sutton, Daniels, Monthe; Scott-Morriss, Pett, Norburn, Robson; Chilvers; Fondop, Kavanagh

Barnsley's comfortable victory over Aldershot was a great first step in their bid to reverse their fortunes, and likely to continue with a full-strength XI in search of another win, we back them to get over the line in a tough game on Wednesday.

#1579. Much-improved Newcastle stop the rot with a 1-1 draw at Fulham - but 'slapstick' defending and wasteful finishing will leave Matthias Jaissle rueing a missed opportunity, writes CRAIG HOPE

Published: 12:52 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:24 EST, 7 November 2026

Just when Newcastle looked set for victory after Jacob Murphy had borrowed Amar Dedic's bow to arrow them into a late lead, they turned the weapon on themselves.

After a week in which Dedic, Bosnia's answer to Robin Hood, had made headlines when pursued by police for wandering around the Northumberland countryside with his hunting gear, the Geordies were ready to rob the good folk of west London after Murphy found the target ten minutes from time.

Less than three minutes later and they were picking the arrow from their own foot. William Osula failed to protect possession and allowed Fulham to enter the penalty area. Then, with the ball bouncing around the goalmouth, it was home substitute Rodrigo Muniz who pounced to punish Newcastle's scruffy defending.

'Slapstick', visiting boss Matthias Jaissle later called it.

The German also said that his team deserved to win but you got the impression he was relieved to emerge without defeat, especially as the performance was improved on the back of a run of four losses in five.

Newcastle's second-half spirit also showed a response to a week of noise centred on dressing-room unrest, not to mention Dedic's police drama.

Jacob Murphy thought he had won it for Newcastle after scoring late on at Craven Cottage

Rodrigo Muniz netted moments later after sloppy defending from Newcastle, earning a 1-1 draw

Matthias Jaissle's side were much improved but must cut out the errors to win matches

And Jaissle was right in that his team could have left with three points had master archer Harvey Barnes not missed a hat-trick of chances.

Fulham (4-2-3-1): Leno 7; Castagne 6 (Tete 77, 5), Affengruber 6, Bassey 6, Robinson 5; Berge 6, Charles 6; Bobb 6 (Sessegnon 78, 6), King 7 (Palacios 72, 5), Iwobi 6; Garcia 4 (Muniz 65, 8)

Subs not used: Lecomte, Andersen, Hugo Larsson, Manuel Angel, Kevin

Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 7; Dedic 6, Thiaw 7 (Schar 85, 6), Burn 7, Hall 6; Nico Gonzalez 5 (Miley 61, 6), Steur 7 (Fernandez-Pardo 74, 5); Murphy 8, Wissa 6 (Willock 61, 5), Barnes 6; Osula 5 (Elanga 85)

Subs not used: Pope, Livramento, Botman, Bazoumana Toure

The winger is the player to whom they'd want those opportunities to fall, too. But twice before half-time, when denied by Bernd Leno from close range, and then again when lashing wide after the break, he failed to give his side the advantage.

Murphy corrected his team-mate's finishing when capitalising on a loose pass from Cesar Palacios and slamming into the bottom corner from 25 yards, but that joy was short-lived.

In truth, there hadn't been much joy to behold all afternoon. The draw keeps both sides in the bottom half of the table, and that is where they will likely stay.

The first half, in particular, had very strong last-on-Match-of-the-Day vibes.

Newcastle thought they had a 33rd-minute lead when Dan Burn stole in at the near post to flick home from Murphy's low cross.

What the officials had spotted at the far post was linebacker Yoane Wissa pinning defender Timothy Castagne, and so playing Burn onside. It was the right call, even if Jaissle disagreed

'I learned that word here, a 'soft' decision. In my eyes, it was not right,' he said. 'But I was pleased with our complete commitment and togetherness.

'We grew through the game and that was excellent, something to build on. We showed the fundamentals.'

Dedic twice came close to creating goals with teasing crosses from the right, and you wondered if he would have mimicked Barnes' trademark archer celebration had they been converted.

He was kept away from the media post-match, but Jaissle did say: 'He played well, right? It (the bow & arrow incident) didn't affect him. He was not aware of the rules. We don't need to make a big deal out of it.'

Fulham's Josh King was included in Thomas Tuchel's England squad on Friday, the club's first Three Lions call-up in eight years. He, however, now needs a scan on a tight groin before learning if he's fit enough to feature.

Did the 19-year-old play like a would-be England international? He was his side's best player in the first half, even if that was a low bar to hurdle. One volley would have raised the roof had it gone in, so sweet was the connection from 20 yards. Lukas Hornicek needed every inch of his 6ft 6in frame to dive and save. And that, too, was a recurring theme, Newcastle's reliance on the big Czech to bail them out when giving up chances.

Like Newcastle, however, Fulham simply weren't good enough to take them.

#1578. Manchester United make crucial Harry Amass decision as January transfer plans emerge

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Manchester United have reportedly made a key decision on Harry Amass ahead of the January transfer window, as they look to resolve ongoing uncertainty at left-back.

The 19-year-old academy graduate had been linked with a permanent departure from Old Trafford during the summer. However, United now appear ready to protect his future by extending his contract, while leaving open the possibility of another loan move.

With injuries affecting the club’s senior defensive options, Amass’ situation could become increasingly important in the coming months.

According to the Evening Standard, Manchester United are preparing to trigger a 12-month extension clause in Amass’ existing contract.

The decision would give the club greater control over the defender’s future and prevent him from approaching the end of his deal without a resolution.

Amass attracted interest from Burnley during the summer after spending time on loan with Sheffield Wednesday and Norwich City. A permanent exit appeared possible, but United ultimately retained the youngster.

The club’s latest reported decision suggests they are not ready to lose control of a player who remains a promising defensive prospect.

United’s situation at left-back has been complicated by fitness concerns involving Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu.

Shaw has struggled with injuries throughout his career, while Dorgu has provided an alternative option when available. Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui can also cover the position, although both are more naturally suited to right-back.

These issues could influence whether Amass stays at Old Trafford or is allowed to leave on loan in January.

Regular first-team football would be valuable for the young defender’s development, but United may be reluctant to weaken their depth while senior players remain unavailable.

A temporary move remains a possibility if United believe Amass would benefit from more regular playing time elsewhere.

His previous loan spells offered opportunities to gain senior experience, although an injury interrupted his time at Norwich City last season.

United must now balance his development against their immediate need for defensive cover. Extending his contract would give the club additional flexibility to make that decision without risking his longer-term value.

The situation could also affect United’s plans for recruiting another left-back, particularly if the club decide they need a more established option.

United’s reported decision to extend Amass’ contract would provide greater security over his future, but it does not guarantee that he will remain in the first-team squad for the rest of the season.

A January loan could still make sense if Shaw and Dorgu are fit enough to provide cover. If injuries continue, however, Amass may have an opportunity to establish himself at Old Trafford.

#1577. How Mauricio Pochettino really feels about Man Utd job revealed after Michael Carrick sack update

By Lewis Blain | 10 Nov 2026 07:05

Mauricio Pochettino could emerge as a leading contender to become Manchester United's next manager if Michael Carrick is dismissed.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss is currently in charge of the United States Mens National Team (USMNT), but reports suggest he would be 'interested' in returning to the Premier League.

With Red Devils chiefs expected to make a decision on Carrick's future during the international break, Pochettino's stance could become increasingly significant.

According to talkSPORT, Pochettino would be keen on taking charge at Old Trafford should United decide to part ways with Carrick.

The Argentine signed a contract extension to remain with the USMNT until the next World Cup in 2030, but his name is expected to feature prominently in the club's search for a replacement.

The Athletic's David Ornstein has also revealed that United expect a managerial change before their next fixture against Liverpool, and that work is already underway on potential replacements.

Pochettino, 54, is among the candidates expected to be considered, alongside former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe and ex-Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann.

United have yet to officially confirm a decision on Carrick, but his position has become increasingly difficult to defend after a disappointing start to the campaign.

The Red Devils are 18th in the Premier League with only eight points from ten matches, having won just once in the competition this season.

Although Carrick rescued a point against Aston Villa with a dramatic 4-4 draw at the weekend, United's hierarchy are expected to hold further discussions before deciding whether to make a change ahead of the trip to Anfield.

Pochettino would represent a considerable upgrade on Carrick in terms of managerial experience, having previously worked at Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea.

He is arguably a more attractive appointment than Howe, too, given his experience of competing at the highest level and his familiarity with the demands of managing a major Premier League club.

However, whoever replaces Carrick will inherit largely the same problems.

United's squad remains unbalanced, with significant holes to fill and inconsistency across several positions, including left-back, out wide and up front. A change in the dugout might provide an immediate lift, but it will not suddenly resolve those obvious weaknesses.

Pochettino could offer a clearer tactical identity and greater experience, but he would need time, and more importantly, substantial investment to turn United into genuine challengers again.

Ultimately, appointing a proven manager is an important first step, but the club's recruitment and long-term planning must improve if another managerial change is to deliver lasting success.

#1576. Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal

Overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

It was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it quickly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

Both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”

It was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another new signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

This was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also said the 3-0 loss represented a “big lesson” for his players.

“There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta said. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

“It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

“It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

“Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta said. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

“It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, said. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”

Two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

When you miss chances like we did it becomes impossible. I want to congratulate Brighton for what they’ve done. It’s a big lesson for us to learn. If I have to describe how the team has played and competed in the last six or seven weeks, has been expectational but today has been a big lesson.

A very disappointing result and performance. Full credit to Brighton the manner they went about the game, they were a different gear from us. We didn’t do the basics right for long periods, especially in the first half. We didn’t win enough duels, and any second balls and that stretches you.

We were poor technically when we had the ball in our own half, we didn’t apply the principles that you need against a team that wants to press you man to man.

Arteta: "There are certain basics that you need to accomplish in the Premier League that we were very far from. The amount of technical errors we did... we didn't respect any principle of play. We were always on the back foot. They had another edge."

Beating the current champions and maybe the best team in England is something special. The result is nice but the performance is what makes it special, the boys showed real courage, real intensity and they were horrible to play against because we did the basics right.

Intensity, intensity, winning the personal duels...we have to have the belief to compete with the best teams in the league. My players really trust each other on the pitch. If one player is out then another can replace him.

Overall we wanted to be really good in every phase. We needed to be at the highest level. We go game by game. After the international break we have a lot of games. After wins like this we have to stay humble and understand why we had this win. We have to keep on going.

Our 125 anniversary & one of the best days! 💫 pic.twitter.com/YbZLTFPpWN

I thought we showed great intensity, waited for mistakes and punished Arsenal. It was a strong performance, a very complete performance.

We won the ball high up and attacked really fast. After the last two wins we are full of confidence and wanted to finish really strong before the international break.

I feel really good. I can’t complain. I just try to help the team when I can. I really enjoy life in Brighton, I’m loving it.

I know after the international break we play every three days and a lot of the lads are not used to that. It will be tough. I hope we can compete. We have a big squad this season.

Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions in three consecutive seasons.

Everton up to fifth but they made hard work of that against Ipswich’s 10 men, but Thierno Barry’s goal proves the difference. Barry unfortunate that his second did not stand because of a contentious offside check.

One of the outstanding team performances of the season so far from Brighton, and it will take some beating between now and May. Arsenal were loose defensively in open play and from set-pieces, and were smothered by Brighton’s pressing. Arteta’s team beaten for the first time this season and emphatically so. Arsenal’s first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023.

Just three minutes of stoppage time remaining, but Hull are still pushing bodies forward.

Hull are knocking on the door at St James’ Park, and Newcastle are hanging on to their lead rather than pressing for a third goal.

Matt O’Riley has missed two great chances to make it four. Brighton have not given Arsenal a sniff. It will be interesting to hear how stern Arteta is in his post-match assessment.

Kai Havertz shoots straight at the goalkeeper when clean through, and that is surely Arsenal’s last chance of an unlikely comeback gone. Brighton have pushed Arsenal back for much of the season half, they have not been sitting on a lead.

At St James’ Park, Hull have pulled a goal back through Cho to set up a nervy finish for Newcastle.

The forward is shown a second yellow card for diving, and Ipswich’s hopes appear to be dwindling at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

What a farcical five minutes we have had, from an absurd disallowed goal for Everton to a ridiculous red card for Abdul Fatawu, banished for a second bookable offence - which was diving. Arsenal undone from a corner, swung to the back post and Chema Andres rose above everyone to head home.

This is a remarkable performance by Brighton, who have battered and bullied the champions from the start. Three-nil, and they have even beaten Arsenal at their own game by scoring a set-piece.

I am struggling to remember the last time Arsenal were overrun and outplayed as comprehensively as this. It’s a thrashing.

A storming response to a bad night at Leeds from Newcastle, and it looks like being a long afternoon for Hull. Two down in seven minutes.

The second came when Sven Botman came away with the ball just inside his own half. On both occasions Harvey Barnes provided the assist. A short, intricate pass to Willock inside the box and then a surging, twisting run from the halfway line and the perfectly timed pass to Lewis Hall who stroked a first time shot into the bottom corner.

Hull have been outfought so far which is precisely the response Newcastle’s manager had demanded.

The home team are pressing high and all over Arsenal in the early stages. Raya has just made a save to deny Kostoulas.

Brighton have started brilliantly against the champions. They are hunting like wolves, pressing Arsenal with remarkable intensity. We have played seven minutes and I don’t think the ball has left Arsenal’s half.

Big chance for Everton to take the lead, but after great skill to turn his man at the edge of the box Brennan Johnson shoots wide with only the goalkeeper to beat.

The perfect start for Newcastle with all their injuries: Joe Willock has put the home side in a strong position against Hull with a clean strike inside three minutes.

We are under way at the Amex, St James’ Park and the Hill Dickinson.

Another famous face in the stands at Hill Dickinson Stadium today but this time it’s not about politicians. Wayne Rooney is here to watch his boyhood club and he will be hoping Everton can go into the international break unbeaten. An extra special cheer too before kick-off for Jarrad Branthwaite, who has just been called up for England duty. Plenty of Premier League clubs would like to sign Branthwaite, if they were given half a chance, but David Moyes has made it quite clear that Branthwaite: “Isn’t for sale - I want to keep my best players.”

He was not part of the match-day squad at Sunderland but Ben White’s injury has opened up a place, and Dowman fully deserves it after his two goals against Ipswich in the League Cup. Sam Dean has the story of his rise to stardom as well as what Arsenal are doing to nurture such a special talent.

Brighton are wearing a special “125 anniversary” kit today, to mark 125 years since the club was formed in 1901. It’s inspired by the colours of their first ever kit, which means an all-blue shirt, pale gold shorts and dark socks. Personally I would not allow such nonsense. But I don’t make the rules.

Spurs scored two late goals to salvage some pride against Aston Villa, but it is another defeat for Roberto De Zerbi’s team who have two points from five games. This Emi Buendia screamer put the game out of reach.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd

It has been a term tossed around liberally at Newcastle United since Matthias Jaissle arrived as manager, but what does “vertical football” actually mean?

It is the new buzzword in football analysis, the latest fashionable phrase to describe a “new” style of football, and it has been referenced multiple times by both Jaissle and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, since the German coach’s appointment last month.

For some of us of a certain age, vertical football just seems like clever new terminology to describe an old idea.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; L Miley, Botman, Thiaw, Hall; Steur, Willock; Murphy, Fernandez-Pardo, Barnes; Wissa

Subs: Pope, Schar, Bamba, Toure, Thompson, Pivas, Salia, M Miley, Mills

Subs: Phillips, Gelhardt, Hjerto-Dahl, McNair, Stroud, Gourna, Iroegbunam, Vaz, Cho

We are getting to the stage where we really need to start asking questions about Tino Livramento’s injury record.

The right back was due to start for Newcastle against Hull City this afternoon – his first start since April – but has picked up another injury.

That will surely mean he is out of the England squad for the Nations League having also picked up a tournament-ending injury at the World Cup in the summer before the first group game.

Livramento only played 17 Premier League games for Newcastle last season, scuppering his chances of a summer move to Arsenal, missing huge chunks of the season with groin and hamstring issues.

Injuries are already cutting deep into the Newcastle squad, with four teenagers on the bench for the visit of Hull. None have played in the first team before and three of them – Michael Mills, Mason Miley and Kyrian Thompson are just 17–years-old.

Newcastle wanted a younger team this season but not this young. It was interesting to hear Matthias Jaissle talk before the game. He knows how tough this season could be with so little experience in the side.

Everton XI: Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Branthwaite, Tarkowski, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Grealish, Dewsbury-Hall, Johnson; Barry

Subs: Scherpen, Furlong, Greaves, Florentino, Nunez, Akpom, Flemming, Philogene, Maeda

Lewis Dunk is a surprise absentee for Brighton, it can only be because of injury, and Hurzeler has preferred Diego Gomez to the lively Yalcouye who was very threatening at Old Trafford and Coventry. He could be a handful off the bench.

Good news for Arsenal: Jurrien Timber is finally fit enough to start a match again. This is his first start since mid-March and his return is timely, given the absence of Ben White through injury. It’s also a first Premier League start for Arsenal for Bruno Guimaraes, who comes into the midfield after his impressive performance off the bench at Sunderland last weekend.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Bruno G, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Tzolis

The one he wore in Only Fools and Horses episode Yuppy Love. Of course, Bloom could actually talk about his wealth rather than one of those old five pound notes he found the other day...

Very excited for this one today. Arsenal have won all seven of their matches so far. Only once before in their history have they won their first eight games of a season - that was in 1903, when they were playing in the Second Division as Woolwich Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/iNBxoHl4Gc

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.
